newsitem.title: UK: S&P cuts Powergen CP rating to A1.
newsitem.headline: S&P cuts Powergen CP rating to A1.

text.p: LONDON -- Standard & Poor's said on Monday it had lowered Powergen Plc's commercial paper rating to A1 from A1 plus.
"The rating change is part of an ongoing review of the generation sector in the U.K. which has resulted in a number of rating downgrades in the sector to date," S&P said in a statement.
S&P said the downgrade reflected the increasing competition in the wholesale generation market in England and Wales and the consequent reduced market power of Powergen.
"The rating change also reflects the increased risks of Powergen's strategy to expand overseas," it added.

"The company continues to enjoy a strong market position in the UK, particularly in the price-setting non-baseload sector of the market where the two generation companies (the other being National Power rated A/A1/Negative) are still setting pool price much of the time."
But S&P said the trend was negative, and Powergen's market share of output has fallen from 28 percent to around 22 percent in the current year.
"There is potential that the generators will need to bid increasingly more aggressively to retain market share and this could lead to revenue erosion."

S&P said Powergen's overseas expansion currently embracds projects in Australia, Germany, Hungary, Indonesia, India and Portugal but the strategy of expansion was to continue with several other countries designated as target markets.

It added that the series of share buybacks announced to date is increasing the company's financial risk and Standard & Poor's expects pressure from investors for Powergen to make greater use of balance sheet leverage either to return value or seize further remunerative opportunities.

"Consequently we expect coverage ratios to fall from historic levels but cash flows will remain relatively strong and Powergen will retain a relatively high degree of financial flexibility to react to adverse circumstances," Standard & Poor's said.
